tpms.when: 2017–2018 with the Tire Pressure Monitor (TPM), which uses sensors in the wheels
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the label in the driver's door opening.
On the iDrive screen, open Vehicle info, then Vehicle status, then choose Perform reset.
Start the engine but stay parked.
Choose Perform reset again so the car stores the pressures you just set.
Drive off. After a short time above about 19 mph, the reset finishes by itself. The wheels show gray on the screen while it works.
When the wheels turn green and the screen says the Tire Pressure Monitor is active, the reset is done.
tpms.note: Reset after every pressure adjustment and every tire or wheel change. If the wheels stay gray on the status screen, the system may have a fault and should be checked by a qualified shop. If the tire pressure light flashes for about a minute when you start the car and then stays on, the warning system itself has a fault. A reset won't fix it; have it checked.

tpms.when: 2017–2018 cars whose status screen shows the Flat Tire Monitor (FTM) instead
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the label in the driver's door opening.
On the iDrive screen, open Vehicle info, then Vehicle status, then choose Perform reset.
Start the engine but stay parked.
Choose Perform reset again to start the setup. The pressures you just set become the reference the system watches.
Drive off. The setup finishes while you drive; if you stop partway, it carries on next time you drive.
tpms.note: Do this after correcting tire pressures and after any tire or wheel change. Do not do it while driving with snow chains fitted. This system cannot spot all four tires slowly losing air together, so keep checking pressures yourself. If the light flashes for about a minute at startup and then stays on, the system has a fault that a reset won't fix.

notes: Checked in the 2017 and 2018 owner's manuals. The owner's manuals we opened show the service (Condition Based Service) items on the screen but give no driver reset for the oil service, so no oil steps are listed here.
